annotation.authors_or_issuer: Fiesler, C.; Beard, N.; Keegan, B.C.
key_provisions_or_claims: Prohibitions on scraping, bots and spiders are very common in social media TOS (analysis of 116 sites).
TOS provisions are ambiguous, inconsistent and lack context, and do not distinguish tools like robots, crawlers and spiders.
Legal status of TOS violations under the CFAA is unsettled, though recent cases (hiQ v. LinkedIn) suggest public data scraping may not violate it.
Ethical decision-making for data collection should go beyond TOS and consider contextual factors of the data source and research.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper analysing data-collection (scraping, bot, spider) prohibitions in the terms of service of 116 social media sites, alongside US legal context (CFAA) and research ethics. Finds provisions common but ambiguous and inconsistent; argues researchers' ethical decisions should look beyond TOS to contextual factors.
annotation.title_clean: No Robots, Spiders, or Scrapers: Legal and Ethical Regulation of Data Collection Methods in Social Media Terms of Service
annotation.title_en: No Robots, Spiders, or Scrapers: Legal and Ethical Regulation of Data Collection Methods in Social Media Terms of Service
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the Fourteenth International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2020)
